pnl_attribution_test_frtb_pat.text: `rates_pnl_attribution` explains where interest-rate P&L came from: it multiplies the P&L per +1bp at each key-rate tenor (`key_rate_sensitivities`) by the realised yield move at that tenor (`yield_moves_bp`) and sums across the ladder. Its question is "how much of my rates P&L came from each tenor?" `pnl_attribution_test_frtb_pat` answers a different question: "does my risk model's P&L track the full-revaluation P&L closely enough?" It takes two daily series, `risk_theoretical_pnl` and `hypothetical_pnl`, and compares them using a Spearman rank correlation and a volatility ratio. It then assigns a Basel traffic-light zone using thresholds set by the Basel Committee and not parameterised. So the first breaks P&L down by tenor, while the second tests the quality of a model's P&L against a benchmark.

explain.text: `rates_pnl_attribution` breaks interest-rate P&L down by key-rate tenor. For each tenor, you give it the P&L per +1bp move (`key_rate_sensitivities`) and the realised yield move in basis points (`yield_moves_bp`). It multiplies each pair and sums across the ladder, so total rates P&L is the sum of the tenor contributions. Because the contributions are additive, you can see how much each part of the curve added or subtracted. You can optionally pass `tenor_names` to label the tenors; otherwise they default to `tenor_0` and so on.

when.text:
`rates_pnl_attribution` (Rates Pnl Attribution) fits when you want to break interest-rate P&L down by key-rate tenor.

- You have P&L per +1bp move at each tenor (`key_rate_sensitivities`) and the realised yield move in basis points at each tenor (`yield_moves_bp`), and you want the total rates P&L as their sum across the ladder.
- You want to see which parts of the curve drove the result, since the contributions are additive across tenors.
- You want readable output, using `tenor_names` to label tenors instead of the default `tenor_0, ...`.
- Other risk drivers, such as FX, credit or volatility, are handled separately, so you only need the rates piece.

If your need is different, `credit_pnl_attribution` covers credit P&L by issuer / curve, and `fx_pnl_attribution` covers FX P&L across currency pairs.
